html:
Abebe Bikila was an Ethiopian runner who won the marathon at the 1960 Olympics in Rome running barefoot. He was the first black African to win an Olympic gold medal, and four years later he became the first person to win the Olympic marathon twice.

He was a soldier in the Imperial Guard of Emperor Haile Selassie and was trained by a Swedish coach, Onni Niskanen. In Rome he ran through the night streets and finished near the Arch of Constantine in a world best time. The win carried extra weight because Fascist Italy had invaded Ethiopia in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War only 25 years before.

At the Tokyo Olympics in 1964, wearing shoes and only weeks after an operation to remove his appendix, he won again, in another world best.

In 1969 a car crash left him paralysed, and he went on to compete in archery in wheelchair games. He died in 1973, aged 41. He opened the way for the great East African distance runners who followed.
